{
  "research_question": "How does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm yielded the highest success rate (0.7798) and shortest mean Time-to-Target (2.56s), outperforming all other groups.",
    "The 'Sham' group demonstrated the poorest performance, with the lowest success rate (0.2733) and the longest mean Time-to-Target (4.68s).",
    "Path Efficiency was highest in 'Bright Visual Only' (0.5036) and 'Combined' (0.5022), while 'Sham' had the lowest efficiency (0.3084).",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) was highest in 'Combined' (0.3994), suggesting greater path variability or exploration compared to 'Sham' (0.2360), despite 'Combined' having the fastest target acquisition.",
    "Average Speed was highest in 'Combined' (12.83) and 'Bright Visual Only' (12.68), whereas 'Sham' mice moved significantly slower (10.74).",
    "Success rates varied widely across paradigms, ranging from 0.2733 (Sham) to 0.7845 (Bright Visual Only), with 'Dim Visual Only' and 'ICMS Only' showing intermediate success rates around 0.68."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "The most striking difference is in the Success metric, where the 'Sham' group (0.2733) fails significantly compared to the 'Bright Visual Only' group (0.7845), a difference of over 0.50.",

    "Path Efficiency is notably lower in 'Sham' (0.3084) compared to visual stimulation groups (~0.50), suggesting that without stimulation or with sham stimulation, mice take much less direct paths.",
    "Angular Dispersion is highest in the 'Combined' condition (0.3994) compared to 'Sham' (0.2360), implying that while combined stimulation leads to faster success, it may also result in more variable or less straight trajectories compared to the sham condition."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Stimulation paradigms significantly alter navigation behavior. The 'Combined' paradigm appears most effective for rapid task completion (lowest Time-to-Target) and high success rates, though it exhibits higher angular dispersion. The 'Sham' condition results in poor performance across all metrics, particularly in success and path efficiency, indicating that the baseline state without effective stimulation leads to inefficient and infrequent target acquisition.",

    "The 'Path Efficiency' metric has a very high standard deviation (0.4667) relative to the mean (0.4745), suggesting a highly skewed distribution that the mean alone may not fully capture.",
    "Sample sizes vary considerably across paradigms (from 3,323 to 48,846), which could influence the precision of the mean estimates, although the large N generally ensures reasonable power."
  ],
